predecessors.note: 'three commanderies were established in its place: Lelang, Lintun, and Zhenfan' (Four Commanderies page). The site is unknown; the Zhenfan page has a northern theory (eastern Liaodong) and a preferred southern one (Gyeongsang, Chungcheong, Jeolla).

successors.note: 'In 82 BCE, Zhenfan was absorbed into Lelang' (Four Commanderies page; Bowman: 'Zhenfan into Lelang').

capitals.name: Sa county (霅縣, site unknown)
capitals.note: 'ruled from the Sa county, which was 3,000 km from Chang'an'; the page does not locate it. The dot is a placeholder in the middle of the Gyeonggi placeholder region.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, and the least certain placement of the batch: the page says 'Its territorial jurisdiction is unclear', lists fifteen unnamed counties and has two theories (north: 'almost same as the eastern part of Liaodong Commandery'; south, preferred: Gyeongsang, Chungcheong or Jeolla). Gyeonggi (the Han River basin, 'south of Lelang' per Bowman) is the researcher's compromise; a reviewer who prefers the southern theory should widen it. No area on the page.

ledger.note: 108 BCE: the Han found Zhenfan. 'In 108 BCE, the Zhenfan Commandery was established under Youzhou by the Han dynasty.' The year is the page's (the Four Commanderies page has 107); the land is a placeholder, confidence 1.

ledger.note: 82 BCE: Zhenfan is abolished into Lelang. 'In 82 BCE, Zhenfan Commandery was abolished'; Bowman (reference list): 'In 82 BCE Lintun was merged into Xuantu, and Zhenfan into Lelang.' The land taken over is as uncertain as the commandery's site.

wars.name: Han conquest of Wiman Joseon
wars.outcome: The Han destroy Wiman Chosŏn in 108 BCE and set up Lelang, Lintun and Zhenfan.
wars.note: Zhenfan's land is not named in any account of the war on the pages opened.

notes: Colony dossier for a commandery whose place nobody knows; the Gyeonggi region is a placeholder at confidence 1, and the rendering agent may reasonably leave Zhenfan undrawn (the dossier still carries its 26 years, its caption, and the 82 BCE absorption into Lelang). Sources disagree: the Zhenfan and Lintun pages say 108 BCE, the Four Commanderies page 107 BCE. The page cites Bowman, Columbia Chronologies, for the 82 BCE merger.
